exactQuestion: Does strong volume/revenue momentum coexistence with realized-price compression constitute a material contradiction that must remain gating?
whyItMatters: The routing queue assigns unresolved_material_contradiction to Deep Resolver; leaving a compatible volume/price tradeoff unresolved would create a false sovereign exception and duplicate root-owner underwriting work.
lawfulFallbacks: Preserve realized-price compression as a non-gating underwriting risk for Council Alpha.
Reopen Resolver only if materially new evidence makes the claims mutually exclusive or changes the input signature.
successCondition: Adjudicate whether the two observations can coexist without weakening either fact, and return remaining numeric underwriting to Council Alpha.

disposition.finding: Strong volume/revenue momentum and realized-price compression are economically compatible, not mutually exclusive. Higher treated volume can increase aggregate revenue while net realized price per unit declines because of mix, rebates, access terms or pricing pressure. Preserve both observations; do not collapse them into a one-direction growth narrative.
disposition.remainingRisk: Pricing/reimbursement pressure may offset some volume growth and therefore remains a material non-gating underwriting risk.
disposition.directive: Deterministic reconciliation should consume this resolved contradiction disposition, clear unresolved_material_contradiction for LLY when no independent unresolved contradiction remains, preserve the price-compression risk, and leave factor/risk/confidence construction to Council Alpha.

evidenceBasis.finding: Council Beta reports no contradictions and treats pricing/reimbursement pressure as a non-gating risk; its structural and red-team perspectives recommend Council Alpha next.
Fresh SEC-filed evidence adds cash-flow, investment and debt facts, reports no contradiction, and explicitly retains Alpha authority over numeric underwriting.

antiRepeat.changedStrategy: Adjudicate the semantic compatibility of the routed volume/price claims using the newest Beta and SEC-backed Scout lineage instead of repeating source acquisition or underwriting.

learning.newLesson: A tradeoff between aggregate growth and per-unit price compression is not inherently a contradiction; reconciliation should distinguish compatible mixed signals from mutually exclusive claims.
